title: Fraud in the Depot
briefing: A depot manager has been claiming the same fuel receipts at two depots for a year. Total about 85,000. Two colleagues noticed and said nothing.
Finance asks the risk team to lead the control review.

evidence.title: How it worked
evidence.body: Expense claims were approved by the depot manager's own deputy. No duplicate check across depots. Receipts were scanned images.

evidence.title: The colleagues
evidence.body: Both say they 'didn't want to cause trouble' and didn't know the speak-up line existed.

questions.prompt: Which control failures enabled the fraud?

options.label: Approval by a subordinate (no real segregation of duties)
Colleagues didn't know how to raise concerns
Receipts were scanned images
options.feedback: Scans are normal; the missing duplicate check is the gap.

options.label: Independent approval above a threshold, automated duplicate checks, a publicised speak-up channel, and recovery of the money
options.feedback: Fixes all three gaps and deals with the case properly.

options.label: Discipline the two colleagues who knew and stayed silent, so everyone across the depots sees that silence has consequences
options.feedback: Punishing silence teaches people to stay silent.

options.label: Recover the money and dismiss the manager: one dishonest person, not a control failure
options.feedback: The controls that allowed it remain.

options.label: The Audit Committee and external auditors, with the control review, and the police if required
options.feedback: Fraud is a governance matter, not just HR.

options.label: HR and the manager's line director, keeping it confidential while the disciplinary process runs
options.feedback: Too narrow for a control failure.

options.label: Handle it within Finance and HR to protect the depot's reputation and the investigation

questions.prompt: How do you address the colleagues' silence?

options.label: Talk with them, find out what stopped them, and use it to fix the speak-up process
options.feedback: Their answer is the most useful evidence.

options.label: Remind them formally of their duty to report, without a disciplinary record this time
Leave them out of it: the investigation is about the manager, not the people around him

lesson: Fraud exploits missing segregation, missing checks and silent colleagues. Fix all three, and learn from the silence rather than punish it.

escalation.text: Nobody from risk picked up "Fraud in the Depot" in time. The executive team handled it alone, late and without a plan, and the damage spread.
